segments.t: At the veterinary clinic, the vet gently speaks with Arlette about her beloved dog's passing while Jean Gabin stays by her side. We will hear it in French first, so don't worry about catching every word.
Il est mort dans son sommeil.
J'ai réservé une place au cimetière.
Let's go back through it. The vet explains the situation.
Il est mort dans son sommeil.
'He died in his sleep.' The vet assures her it was peaceful. The verb meaning 'to be' pairs naturally with the noun for 'sleep' in everyday conversation.
'It is the best death.' He tries to make her feel better. In spoken French, the little word before 'the next word' drops its final vowel and attaches with an apostrophe.
'And for us too.' He adds that it is ideal for anyone. The adverb meaning 'also' gives the reply its conversational emphasis.
'It is true, thank you.' Arlette agrees sadly. A short, idiomatic conversational reply that keeps the exchange moving naturally.
J'ai réservé une place au cimetière.
'I reserved a place at the cemetery.' He took care of the arrangements. The verb meaning 'to have' pairs naturally with the noun for 'seat' in everyday conversation.
'They will come pick him up.' He explains the next step. The clause hinges on the everyday verb meaning 'to come'.
'Can I do anything else?' He offers further assistance. In everyday spoken French, rising intonation on 'can' at the end is enough to turn the sentence into a question.
'It is fine, thank you.' She declines politely. A short, idiomatic conversational reply that keeps the exchange moving naturally.
'Can you leave us?' She asks for some privacy. Inverting the verb and pronoun around 'can you' creates a crisp, polished question.
'Of course.' The vet respects her wish. The adverb meaning 'well' gives the reply its conversational emphasis.
'He is really gone.' She realizes the finality of it. This conversational past tense combines a helper verb with the past verb form for 'gone'.
'Goodbye, my dog.' She says a heartfelt farewell. Notice how 'to see again' leads directly into the noun meaning 'dog'. Let's listen to the whole scene again.
Il est mort dans son sommeil.
J'ai réservé une place au cimetière.
And that's it for this scene. When you watch the episode, listen out for the exchange around the best death, and for the words meaning 'to be' and 'dead'. You'll catch them now. See you next time.

lines.fragment: Gardez à l'esprit qu'il est mort dans son sommeil.
C'est la meilleure façon de mourir pour un chien.
J'ai réservé une place pour lui au cimetière pour chiens d'Asnières.
Je les préviens, ils viendront le chercher.
S'il y a quoi que ce soit que je puisse faire pour vous...
Pouvez-vous nous laisser, s'il vous plaît?
